caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:pvc-12
attempts.entry_title: V1 responses to illusory corner-folds (Martinez-Conde et al. 2019)
attempts.summary: The paper's central finding held up in this data: V1 responses to Vasarely's illusory corner-folds grow as the corner sharpens, the sharpest folds respond significantly more than the flattest, and the relation to corner angle is not linear. Against a luminance Edge the significance tests held, but matching each fold to an Edge contrast was a borderline miss, and the RMS contrast fit failed, as the paper gives no display black level. Similarity to a difference-of-Gaussians model could not be tested without the model's output. Equal baseline across stimuli and some Table 1 values did not reproduce, and depend on baseline square placements the Methods leave open. The Star results rest on 12 of the paper's 30 neurons.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Martinez-Conde, McCamy, Troncoso, Otero-Millan and Macknik (2019) on CRCNS pvc-12, which holds per neuron and condition the spike rate maps and stimuli of V1 neurons recorded in two monkeys viewing the Square and Edge, Star and Corners stimuli. It compares the spike rate difference at the corner-fold midpoints across fold angles, the responses along the folds (Table 1), the baselines across stimuli, and the comparison with the Edge. The spike times, eye positions and eye time maps are not in the data set, and 15 of 27 Star recordings cannot be placed on their stimulus.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Martinez-Conde et al. (2019) from CRCNS pvc-12

outcomes.statement: Of 118 V1 neurons recorded from two monkeys (102 from monkey J, 16 from monkey A), 60 were discarded for technical problems and 58 analysed; 7 were tested in all three conditions, 11 in two and 40 in one, giving 25 neurons for Square and Edge, 30 for Star and 28 for Corners.
outcomes.quote: Thus, we present data from 58 neurons total. ... we were able to test all three conditions in 7 neurons, two conditions in 11 neurons, and a single condition in 40 neurons out of the 58.
outcomes.notes: The spreadsheet V1_Vasarely_data_SMC.xlsx has 58 rows, the paper's total, but 5 mark no condition and have no files, so the files hold 53 neurons (49 from monkey J, 4 from A), as the data descriptor says. By folder they give 22 Square and Edge, 29 Star and 26 Corners neurons, with 7 in three conditions, 10 in two and 36 in one (measured, in the claim's order). Counting the two ABS files of the Star folder as the Corners recordings they are gives 22, 27 and 26, with 7, 8 and 38. No per-condition count is the paper's (25, 30, 28); of the overlap counts only the 7 in all three conditions matches. The 118 recorded and 102 and 16 per monkey cannot be checked, as the discarded neurons are not in the data set.
deviations: Neurons are identified across conditions by the cell code without its trailing letter (date, monkey and cell number), as the spreadsheet lists them; nothing else in the files confirms it.

outcomes.statement: Each experimental condition required at least 10,000 spikes, and the mean number of spikes per condition was 35,998 (STD 25,981).
outcomes.quote: The minimum number of spikes required to complete each experimental condition was 10,000 (the mean and STD of number of spikes per condition was 35,998 ± 25,981).
outcomes.notes: The files hold no spike count map and no spike times. The stored image is the spike rate per 1 ms eye-time sample, and only one file of 77 (ABC050900J1A) also holds the eye time map, from which its count is 15,644 spikes. Neither reading of the criterion can be computed for the others. The data set's documentation (docs/crcns_pvc-12_data_description.pdf) names no other file that holds them.

outcomes.statement: Absolute baseline activity did not differ significantly across the three visual stimuli (Square and Edge, Star, Corners).
outcomes.source: Results, Strength of neuronal responses to corner-folds varies parametrically with fold angle, paragraph 1; S4 Fig
outcomes.quote: Importantly, we found no significant differences in absolute baseline activity across the different visual stimuli presented ( S4 Fig ).
outcomes.notes: Under the main baseline reading (for each stimulus the placement closest to the files' BaseActivity, centred on the corners for Square and Edge, inside them for the Star, the bottom corners of the ROI for Corners) the medians are 6.72 (Square and Edge, n = 22), 1.90 (Star, n = 12) and 2.57 spikes/s (Corners, n = 26), and all three readings find a difference at 0.05; (a) Square and Edge against Corners, BH p = 0.037 (against Star 0.065), (b) Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.025, (c) ANOVA p = 0.004. With the squares centred or inside the corners for both stimuli the difference is larger (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.005 and 0.008). With the files' own BaseActivity (38 of 60 files) no test finds a difference (smallest p 0.109), nor does the main reading on the same 38 files (smallest p 0.060) or with the Corners squares 32 DU further in (0.063); with them 24 DU higher the ANOVA finds one (p = 0.026). The outcome rests on the placement of the baseline squares and on which neurons are included, and the Star group has 12 neurons in place of 30.
deviations: The baseline squares are placed, for each stimulus, where their values come closest to the files' BaseActivity, the authors' own baseline in 38 files; centred on the corners of the circumscribing square for Square and Edge (median difference 0.46 spikes/s against 1.33 inside, n = 9) and inside the corners for the Star (0.39 against 1.30 centred, n = 10). The text says only "at the corners of the ... circumscribing square" (Methods, Visual stimuli). This is an assumption; both placements for both stimuli and the files' values are shown.

The Square and Edge squares centred on the corners run past the authors' 151 DU frame; they are read from the screen maps moved into a frame widened by 16 DU (r of 0.994 or more with the authors' maps inside their frame), averaged over the part on the screen (6 squares in 5 files are partly off it).

The Corners baseline squares are placed at the two bottom corners of the ROI, 8 DU in from each side, in the darkest (1%) area. The text says only "two 1 x 1 DVA (16 x 16 DU) square regions in 0% luminance areas within the ROI (shown in Fig 2C)" (Methods, Corners); Fig 2C is not in the text read. The files' BaseActivity matches none of the three placements tried closely (median difference 0.85 to 2.79 spikes/s). This is an assumption; the other two are shown.
Star results rest on the 12 of 27 Star recordings that hold the authors' aligned map.

outcomes.statement: For every fold (P180, S90, S52, S40), most neurons' midpoint fold responses lie above their absolute baseline activity, and the mass center of each fold's points lies above the line of unit slope, with the mass center's distance from that line increasing as the fold angle decreases.
outcomes.source: Figure 4A legend; Results, Strength of neuronal responses, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: For all folds, most data points and all mass centers fall above the line, indicating a predominance of elevation of midpoint fold response above absolute baseline activity.
outcomes.notes: Under the main baseline reading, neurons above baseline are 18 of 22 (P180), 18 of 22 (S90), 12 of 12 (S52) and 26 of 26 (S40), every mass centre lies above the unit line, and its distance grows from P180 through S90 and S52 to S40 under reading (a) (4.03, 8.39, 19.19, 26.27 spikes/s) and under reading (b), the mean log ratio (0.221, 0.351, 0.916, 1.002). The order under (a) holds under every baseline reading shown; under (b) it fails with the Star squares centred on the corners (S52 1.210 > S40 1.002) and with the Corners squares 32 DU further in (S40 0.837 < S52 0.916).
deviations: Baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).
Star results rest on 12 neurons in place of 30, Corners on 26 in place of 28, Square and Edge on 22 in place of 25.

outcomes.statement: The mean spike rate difference at the fold midpoint decreases with increasing fold angle, from S40 (25.60 spikes/s) through S52 (18.10) and S90 (10.69) to P180 (4.87).
outcomes.quote: The distances in Fig 4B show the clear trend of diminished spike rate difference with increasing corner angle.
outcomes.notes: With the bright S40 fold and the main baseline reading the means are S40 26.27 (SEM 4.29, n = 26), S52 19.19 (3.03, n = 12), S90 8.39 (2.22, n = 22) and P180 4.03 spikes/s (1.18, n = 22); the order holds and S40, S52 and P180 are within tolerance, S90 is 2.30 below 10.69, outside its 1.94. The order holds under every baseline reading shown and on the unsmoothed map, and none puts all four within tolerance (S90 falls outside with the squares centred or inside for both stimuli and with both other Corners placements, P180 and S52 with the files' BaseActivity, S52 and S40 with the main reading on the files that have it, P180 on the unsmoothed map). The two monkey A neurons give P180 -2.94 and S90 -4.44, monkey J 4.72 and 9.68. Before the revision the Square and Edge baseline squares were read partly outside the authors' frame as zeros, which lowered the baseline; corrected, S90 moved from 10.83 to 8.39 and P180 from 6.47 to 4.03, so the value outside tolerance is now S90 in place of P180. On the claims file's answer to this attempt's question the criterion takes the bright S40 fold alone; under the dropped reading with the two S40 folds averaged S40 is 19.09, below S52, and the order fails.
deviations: Baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).

The maps are the authors' (made at 60 ms, smoothed, aligned in their ROI frame); the eye-signal correction and the registration cannot be redone, and 15 Star recordings without the aligned frame cannot be used.

outcomes.statement: The midpoint spike rate difference for S40 is significantly larger than for S90 and for P180, and that for S52 is significantly larger than for P180.
outcomes.source: Results, Strength of neuronal responses, paragraph 1; Figure 4B legend
outcomes.quote: The spike rate difference for S40° was significantly larger than that for fold S90° and P180°, and the spike rate difference for S52° was significantly larger than that for P180°.

statistics.about: S40 against S90, S40 against P180, S52 against P180

outcomes.notes: Rank sum tests with BH correction over six pairs, S40 against S90 p = 0.00028 and against P180 p = 2.1e-06, S52 against P180 p = 0.00014, all in the stated direction; over the three named pairs the same. They hold under every baseline reading shown. Of the other pairs, S52 against S90 is significant (p = 0.011), S40 against S52 (p = 0.36) and S90 against P180 (p = 0.16) are not.
deviations: Star rests on 12 neurons in place of 30.

outcomes.statement: The population-average spike rate difference maps show neural activity increasing as the corner angle decreases.
outcomes.source: Figure 5; Results, Strength of neuronal responses, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The maps also show that neural activity increased with decreasing corner angles.
outcomes.notes: At the fold midpoints the average maps give S40 26.27, S52 19.19, S90 8.39 and P180 4.03 spikes/s, ordered as claimed; the variant of block means (23.01, 17.15, 7.61, 3.61) gives the same order. The S40 midpoint is the bright fold's, as the claims file says. This repeats fig4b-spike-rate-difference and is not an independent test.
deviations: Corners frames come in two sizes (273 x 209 DU in 20 files, 257 x 193 in 6, printed in the notebook) and are averaged on a common canvas centred on each frame; the midpoints are read in the larger frame.
Baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).

outcomes.statement: Along the Edge, the spike rate difference over the ten 10% luminance blocks has a mean minimum of 7.98, maximum 33.13, mean 20.44 and median 20.77 spikes/s, and 22.01 at the Edge midpoint.
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 1; no sentence states them. The text says only that they are summarized in Table 1 (Results, Responses averaged along the entire fold, paragraph 1).
outcomes.notes: On the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen, under reading (a) (summaries per neuron, then the mean), all five values are within the paper's SEM (measured). On all 22 files three are (minimum 5.78 and median 17.09 fall outside), and under reading (b) on all 22 three are. With the squares inside the corners 2 of 5 are within tolerance on the 22 files and 5 of 5 on the 18 (6.57, 31.59, 18.62, 18.82, 21.15); the Corners placements leave the Edge unchanged. With the files' BaseActivity none is within tolerance, on the 9 neurons of the 22 files and on the 6 of the 18, and the main reading on those 6 also gives none. So the outcome rests on leaving out the four files whose Edge is cut by the screen border and on which neurons are included; on the 18 files the computed placements agree.
deviations: Baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).

In four files (AEC052900J1, AEC070500J2, AEC09010J1C, AEC09040J3B) the 100% end of the Edge is cut by the screen border, so the top blocks there partly sample the black screen. The Methods say the rectangle was sometimes partly off the display "but never its edge" (Methods, Square and edge), so the Edge measures the paper made were on a wholly displayed Edge; the Edge values are taken from the other 18 files. This is an assumption; all 22 are shown.

outcomes.statement: Along P180, the spike rate difference over the ten blocks has a mean minimum of 0.18, maximum 10.28, mean 4.55 and median 4.03 spikes/s, and 4.87 at the midpoint.
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 1; no sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a) four of five values are within tolerance (maximum 10.33, mean 3.61, median 3.03, midpoint 4.03 spikes/s); the minimum, -1.55, is below 0.18 by more than 1.01. Under (b) three are. With the squares inside the corners 3 of 5 are within tolerance, with the files' BaseActivity (9 neurons) 3, with the main reading on those 9 neurons 5, and on the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen 2, so the count moves with the baseline and with the neurons included. The outcome was not reproduced before the revision (one of five, every value but the minimum about 1.5 spikes/s high); the Square and Edge baseline squares had then been read partly outside the authors' frame as zeros, and corrected the baseline is higher.
deviations: P180 is the line parallel to the Edge, 48 DU into the rectangle, from 0% to 100% (Methods, Square and edge); baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).

outcomes.statement: Along the S90 fold of the Square, the spike rate difference over the ten blocks has a mean minimum of 4.36, maximum 14.61, mean 9.22 and median 9.31 spikes/s, and 10.69 at the midpoint.
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 1; no sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (i)(a) two of five values are within tolerance (maximum 13.58 and mean 7.61); the minimum 2.46, median 7.66 and midpoint 8.39 are below the paper's values by more than their SEM (measured). No other reading gives more than two. With the squares inside the corners 1 of 5 is within tolerance and with the files' BaseActivity (9 neurons) 3 of 5 under (ii)(a); the main reading on those 9 neurons gives 5 of 5 under (ii)(a), so the outcome rests on the baseline and on which neurons are included. The outcome was reproduced before the revision (all five under (i)(a)); the Square and Edge baseline squares had then been read partly outside the authors' frame as zeros, and corrected the baseline is higher and every S90 value lower.
deviations: Baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).
The S90 blocks are 7.07 DU long; their samples are now spaced 1.01 DU apart and placed symmetrically about each block's centre.

outcomes.statement: Along the S52 fold of the Star, the spike rate difference over the ten blocks has a mean minimum of 6.26, maximum 25.39, mean 15.66 and median 15.93 spikes/s, and 18.10 at the midpoint.
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 1; no sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (ii)(a), each half of the aligned diagonal summarised as its own ten blocks, all five values are within the paper's SEM (measured); under (i)(a) four are (the minimum 9.08 is above 6.26 by more than 1.33). With the squares centred on the corners for the Star the best is 3 of 5, with the files' BaseActivity (10 neurons) 2, and with the main reading on those 10 neurons 1, so the outcome rests on the Star baseline placement and on 12 neurons in place of 30. The outcome was partially reproduced before the revision, when the Star baseline squares were centred on the corners; the main reading now places them inside the corners, where their values come closest to the files' BaseActivity.
deviations: Star rests on the 12 recordings with the authors' aligned map.
Baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption).

outcomes.statement: Along the S40 fold of Corners, the spike rate difference over the ten blocks has a mean minimum of 9.33, maximum 35.11, mean 22.81 and median 22.83 spikes/s, and 25.60 at the midpoint.
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 1; no sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: With the bright S40 fold under reading (a) all five values are within the paper's SEM. They stay within it with the files' BaseActivity and with the Corners squares 24 DU higher; with the squares 32 DU further in four are, and with the main reading on the 19 files that have BaseActivity three are. On the claims file's answer to this attempt's question the criterion takes the ten blocks along the bright S40 fold alone; under the dropped reading with the two folds averaged at most one of five values was within tolerance.
deviations: Corners baseline squares at the bottom corners of the ROI (assumption).

outcomes.statement: For each fold and the Edge, the spike rate difference at the midpoint does not differ significantly from the mean or the median spike rate difference along the fold or Edge, so the midpoint response represents the whole fold.
outcomes.source: Results, Responses averaged along the entire fold are comparable to those at fold midpoint, paragraph 1; Figure 6
outcomes.quote: We found that the spike rate difference at the corner-fold midpoint was not significantly different from the mean and median spike rate difference along the corner-fold or Edge (Wilcoxon rank sum test, α = 0.05; Fig 6 )
outcomes.notes: None of the ten rank sum tests is significant (p = 0.49 to 0.93), nor any under the other reading of the halves, nor the two Edge tests on the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen (p = 0.70 and 0.95); the midpoint exceeds the block mean or median by a median of -0.08 to 2.39 spikes/s. The paired signed rank test, the variant, finds 3 of 10 significant (S90 against the median p = 0.025, S40 against the mean p = 0.015 and the median p = 0.009). The baseline cancels in these comparisons.
deviations: Star rests on 12 neurons in place of 30.

outcomes.statement: Local RMS contrast along the Edge rises from 0.61 to 0.943 with luminance and is fit by an exponential model, f(l) = -0.34 exp(-0.05 l) + 0.95, with R2 = 0.9983.
outcomes.source: Results, Neuron responses to corner-folds vs. different contrasts along edge, paragraph 1; Figure 7A
outcomes.quote: This resulted in smooth contrasts ranging from 0.61 to 0.943. In order to acquire neural responses to the Edge at equally spaced RMS contrast intervals, we fit the RMS contrast with an exponential model ( R 2 = 0.9983; Fig 7A ).
outcomes.notes: Computed on the luminance of the stimulus image (in percent, black at 0) in the authors' frame, as the median over the 18 Edge files whose Edge is wholly on the screen. Under reading (a), standard deviation over mean, the contrast is 1.98 at 0%, near 0.86 from 25% to 75% and 1.28 at 100% (measured, lowest, highest, a, b, c and R2 of the LAR fit); only c is within tolerance. Under reading (b), standard deviation of luminance scaled to 0 to 1, it rises from 0.013 to 0.449 and only R2 (0.9987) is within tolerance. The text gives the display luminance at one level, 14.07 cd/m2 at 50% (Methods, Square and edge), but not the black level; a contrast that saturates near 0.95 would need a black level above zero, which neither the text nor the files give, and none was tried.
deviations: LAR is implemented as a least absolute residual fit started from a Levenberg-Marquardt least squares fit, standing in for MATLAB's Curve Fitting Toolbox.

outcomes.statement: Neural responses to P180 are roughly equivalent to those to a 50% contrast Edge, while responses to S40 are close to those to a 90% contrast Edge, so sharper corners produce responses equivalent to higher contrasts along a straight edge.
outcomes.source: Results, Neuron responses to corner-folds vs. different contrasts along edge, paragraph 3; Figure 7C
outcomes.quote: Fig 7C shows that neural responses to P180° are roughly equivalent to neural responses to a 50% contrast Edge, while neural responses to S40° are close to neural responses to a 90% contrast Edge.
outcomes.notes: With the Edge from the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen, the Edge response (16 x 16 DU squares on the Edge) ranges from 9.23 spikes/s at 0% luminance to 21.26 at 80%. Under reading (a) the P180 mean (4.03) lies below the whole Edge profile and is nearest the 0% level, not within one step of 50%; S40 (26.27) is nearest 80%, within one step of 90%. Under reading (b) P180 is nearest the lowest RMS level, which the rule accepts, and S40 is nearest the 94.3 level. Measured as a distance from 90, 94.3 is 4.3 away against a step of 3.7, a miss of 0.6, and (b) fails; counted as one level away from the level nearest 90 (90.6), the variant, (b) passes and the claim would be reproduced. The two readings are equally literal, so the outcome is borderline; reading (a) fails clearly, and (b) turns on this choice. Every other baseline reading and the Edge from all 22 files give the same under (a) and (b). The RMS levels are placed with the paper's fitted parameters (luminance 0 to 77.7%), as the claims file says.
deviations: The refit variant of the criterion is not run, because the recomputed contrast is not monotonic in luminance.
The Edge levels at 10% steps are taken at 0%, 10%, and so on to 100%, with 16 x 16 DU squares as for the RMS levels; Fig 7B gives no window for them.

Under reading (b) "within one step of 90%" is measured as a distance from 90 of at most 3.7; one level from the level nearest 90, an equally literal reading, is shown as a variant and passes. This is an assumption the outcome rests on.

The Edge responses come from the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen, as in table1-edge (assumption); baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption); the S40 response is the bright fold's, as the claims file says.

outcomes.statement: Responses to P180 are significantly lower than responses to a 94% contrast Edge, and responses to S40 are significantly higher than responses to an Edge of less than 68% contrast.
outcomes.source: Results, Neuron responses to corner-folds vs. different contrasts along edge, paragraph 3; S2 Table
outcomes.quote: In addition, the neural responses to P180° are significantly lower than the responses to a 94% contrast Edge, and the neural responses to S40° are significantly higher than the responses to an Edge of less than 68% contrast (two sample t -test corrected; S2 Table ).
outcomes.notes: Two-sample t-tests (equal variance) of the fold midpoint differences against the Edge responses of the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen. Under BH over all 40 tests (a), P180 is lower than the Edge at 0.943 (adjusted p = 0.015) and S40 higher than the Edge at 0.610 and 0.647 (both 0.033); BH per fold (b) gives the same (0.0038; 0.022, 0.022), and so does Bonferroni per fold (0.0076; 0.033, 0.045). Bonferroni over 40 tests fails (S40 at 0.610 p = 0.13). With the Edge from all 22 files the claim holds under (a) and (b). Under (a) S40 is also significantly higher at 0.684, 0.721 and 0.758, beyond the paper's "less than 68%", and P180 is lower at every level from 0.647 up.
deviations: The Edge responses come from the 18 files whose Edge is wholly on the screen, as in table1-edge (assumption); baseline placement as in s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption); the S40 response is the bright fold's, as the claims file says.

outcomes.statement: The relationship between corner angle and V1 spike rate difference is parametric but apparently not linear; the paper says it cannot be certain of this, given the few angles tested.
outcomes.quote: In contrast with the previous perceptual data, however, we did not find a linear relationship between corner sharpness and the strength of the neural response.
outcomes.notes: The four means decrease monotonically with angle. A least-squares line (-0.142 spikes/s per degree) leaves S40 4.63 above it (SEM 4.29), S90 6.15 below (SEM 2.22) and P180 2.26 above (SEM 1.18), so by the claims file's SEM rule the relation is non-linear; S90 and P180 lie off the line under every other baseline reading shown. In the variant the slope from 52 to 90 degrees (-0.284) differs from that from 90 to 180 (-0.049) by more than their combined SE; the slopes from 40 to 52 (-0.59 +- 0.44) and from 52 to 90 do not.
deviations: Rests on the baseline placement of s4-baseline-no-difference (assumption); the S40 response is the bright fold's, as the claims file says.

outcomes.statement: The V1 responses as a function of fold angle follow a trend remarkably similar to the output of the difference-of-Gaussians center-surround model of reference [3].
outcomes.source: Figure 7D; Results, Center-surround model vs. V1 neuron responses, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: The two response trends are remarkably similar, suggesting that a) there is little transformation in the neural responses to corner-folds from the retinal/LGN to area V1
outcomes.notes: Needs the output of the difference-of-Gaussians model of reference [3], which the paper shows only as a line in Fig 7D. The paper names no deposited data for it, the data set holds none, and the claims file names no public source. An outside input that is not public is blocked as data_missing (docs/protocol.md, author step 4).

outcomes.statement: Midpoint responses to corner-folds, computed for retina-to-V1 latencies from 1 to 2400 ms, peak around 60 ms across the visual stimuli.
outcomes.source: Methods, Conduction latency; S3 Fig legend
outcomes.quote: Peak responses occurred around 60 ms across visual stimuli
outcomes.notes: Needs spike times and eye positions to rebuild the maps at other latencies. The files hold only the maps made at 60 ms, and the data set's documentation names no other files.

findings.statement: The data set holds 53 neurons, not the 58 the paper analysed. The spreadsheet V1_Vasarely_data_SMC.xlsx lists 58 cells, five of them (050800J1, 062000J1, 072100_C, 062600A2, 09250A1) with no condition marked and no files. Per condition the files hold 22 Square and Edge, 27 Star and 26 Corners recordings, against the paper's 25, 30 and 28.

Two files in the Star folder, ABS042700J2 and ABS051000J3, are recordings with a Corners-type stimulus (their stimulus metadata gives the type CORNERS, triangles 45 DU wide and 60 DU deep), and the spreadsheet marks both cells as tested with the Star. They are not copies of the same cells' Corners files (pixel correlation 0.83 and 0.72).

The data descriptor says the spike rate map file holds image (raw spike counts), smoothed_image and smoothed_image_norm (normalised by eye time). In the files, image is the spike rate per 1 ms eye-time sample (times the eye time it is an integer count, and 98.5% of the pixels with eye time hold values strictly between 0 and 1, in the one file with an eye time map); smoothed_image_norm is absent from 39 of 77 files, and in the 38 that hold it it is smoothed_image minus the file's BaseActivity in 5 (among them the one file with an eye time map, so not normalised by eye time), a linear rescaling of smoothed_image in 21, not a linear function of it in 11 (26% to 77% of the pixels at exactly -1), and non-finite in 1; and most files hold a Standard struct and a norm flag that the descriptor does not mention.

The maps are in gaze coordinates. The receptive-field offset that places them on the stimulus is in no file; the authors' aligned maps (the undocumented Standard struct) are present for all Corners and Square and Edge files but only 12 of 27 Star files, so 15 Star recordings cannot be analysed. The offset differs between conditions of the same neuron by up to about 50 DU, so it cannot be carried across. Standard also holds BaseActivity in 38 of 60 files, with no description of how it was computed; it comes closest to squares centred on the corners of the circumscribing square for Square and Edge (median difference 0.46 spikes/s) and to squares inside them for the Star (0.39), matches neither exactly, and matches no Corners placement tried closely.

No file holds spike times, eye positions or spike count maps, and only one (ABC050900J1A) holds an eye time map, so the spikes per condition, the latency analysis of S3 Fig and any map rebuilt from the recordings cannot be computed.

In four Square and Edge files (AEC052900J1, AEC070500J2, AEC09010J1C, AEC09040J3B) the 100% end of the Edge lies beyond the screen border, where the Methods say the rectangle was sometimes partly off the display "but never its edge".

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells removed (the handover left in the summary cell, which the verifier says it did not use), the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier read the zip's file list, tested the helpers on synthetic inputs (box_mean, the midpoint, the block profile, fit_rigid, the LAR fit, rms_contrast_profile) and did not re-run the notebook. It had no attempt record.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the paper's full text. The verifier re-ran nothing on the data and drew its conclusions from the stored outputs; it read the box_mean code without running it. It found no place where the claims file misreads the paper.

paper_notes.statement: Where are the absolute baseline squares? The text puts four 16 x 16 DU squares "at the corners" of the square circumscribing the Square or the Star, without saying whether they are centred on the corners or drawn inside them, and two for Corners "in 0% luminance areas within the ROI (shown in Fig 2C)" with no position. The choice changes the baseline test across stimuli (a difference at Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.025 under this attempt's main reading, none with the files' BaseActivity) and the Table 1 counts. This attempt takes, per stimulus, the placement closest to BaseActivity (centred for Square and Edge, inside for the Star) and for Corners the ROI's bottom corners. Which placement, and how was BaseActivity computed?

How was the local RMS contrast of Fig 7A computed? From the stimulus luminance in percent neither the standard deviation over the mean nor the standard deviation of luminance scaled to 0 to 1 gives a contrast rising from 0.61 to 0.943. The text gives the display luminance at 50% (14.07 cd/m2) but not the black level, which a contrast saturating near 0.95 would need, and the definition (reference 21) is not in the text read.

The Methods give the Star ROI as 10 x 10 DVA (160 x 160 DU), but the Star's 0% polygon has a circumscribed radius of 150 DU and the authors' Star frame in the files is 321 x 321 DU. The circumscribing square of the Square is given as 8.84 x 8.84 DVA and as 138 x 138 DU; 8.84 DVA is 141.4 DU, the Square's diagonal. The Square and Edge ROI is 9.38 DVA (150 DU) wide, and the baseline squares are said to be within it, but 16 x 16 DU squares centred on the corners of a 138 or 141.4 DU square span 154 to 157 DU, and the files' BaseActivity comes closest to that placement.

entries.name: martinez-conde-2019
entries.title: V1 responses to illusory corner-folds (Martinez-Conde et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Martinez-Conde, McCamy, Troncoso, Otero-Millan and Macknik (2019) on CRCNS pvc-12, which holds per neuron and condition the spike rate maps and stimuli of V1 neurons recorded in two monkeys viewing the Square and Edge, Star and Corners stimuli. It compares the spike rate difference at the corner-fold midpoints across fold angles, the responses along the folds (Table 1), the baselines across stimuli, and the comparison with the Edge. The spike times, eye positions and eye time maps are not in the data set, and 15 of 27 Star recordings cannot be placed on their stimulus.
